questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let A(x, y, z) be a point in xy-plane, which is equidistant from three points (0, 3, 2), (2, 0, 3) and (0, 0, 1). Let B = (1, 4, -1) and C = (2, 0, -2). Then among the statements (S1): triangle ABC is an isosceles right angled triangle and (S2): the area of triangle ABC is 9*sqrt(2)/2
questions.sol_text:
A(x,y,z) Let P(0,3,2), Q(2,0,3), R(0,0,1)
AP = AQ = AR
x^2 + (y - 3)^2 + (z - 2)^2 = (x - 2)^2 + y^2 + (z - 3)^2 = x^2 + y^2 + (z - 1)^2

In xy plane z = 0
So, x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 + 9 = x^2 + y^2 + 1
x = 3

9 + y^2 - 6y + 9 + 4 = x^2 + y^2 + 1
So, A(3,2,0) also B(1,4,-1) & C(2,0,-2)

Now AB = sqrt(4 + 4 + 1) = 3
AC = sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = 3
BC = sqrt(1 + 16 + 1) = sqrt(18)

AB = AC
isosceles triangle & AB^2 + AC^2 = BC^2
right angle triangle

Area of triangle ABC = (1/2) × base × height
= (1/2) × 3 × 3 = 9/2

So only S1 is true
